subject: MedAxis — deployment routing & evidence checklist
messages:
From: Cara Douglass <cara.d@medaxis.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@medaxis.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 12:20:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — deployment constraints and evidence asks

Lukas — thanks for the demo and the clear rundown this morning. Quick recap from our side and the items we need to make a hosting decision: 

- Regulatory context: MedAxis processes PHI for our remote-monitoring product. We need a BAA and SOC2 Type II evidence before we can move to production.
- Preferred hosting: our security team prefers a Private VPC or on-prem option, but we want to understand the delta vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) in terms of evidence, network controls, and timeline.
- Technical constraints: expected steady-state ~200 QPS inference across 10K daily active users, peaks up to 1.2k QPS for short bursts. Average prompt lengths ~150 tokens.
- Key asks: sample SOC2 report (redacted), BAA template, network architecture (how would VPC peering or a private deployment look), KMS/HSM integration details, and an estimate for provisioning time & cost for Dedicated vs Private.

Can you send the checklist/artifacts and confirm whether Redwood can support an on-prem or VPC-hosted private control plane? Also list the minimal evidence your security team typically requires for Dedicated vs Private.

Appreciate it — happy to sync again once we see the materials.

— Cara
Cara Douglass
Head of Security & Privacy
MedAxis Health
cara.d@medaxis.com

Attachments: medaxis-internal-security-notes.pdf (referenced)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Cara Douglass <cara.d@medaxis.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@medaxis.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — deployment constraints and evidence asks

Cara — thanks for the clear list and for the call today. Recap + proposed next steps below.

Recap (short):
- You process PHI and are evaluating Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem.
- Performance target ~200 QPS steady, bursts to ~1.2k QPS.
- Primary blockers: BAA, SOC2 evidence, network controls, and provisioning lead time.

What Redwood will provide immediately: 
- Redacted SOC2 Type II report (PDF) and a SOC2 evidence extract for common controls.
- Our standard BAA template (we can start a draft with MedAxis legal).
- A network diagram showing VPC peering and private control plane options + KMS integration notes.
- A deployment comparison one-pager outlining differences (security controls, operational responsibilities, SLA delta, expected provisioning time / cost).

Questions for you (so we size/propose correctly):
1) Do you require customer-managed HSM for key material or is KMS integration sufficient?
2) For on-prem: do you plan to host inference GPU servers in your data center, or would you prefer Redwood-managed appliances installed behind your firewall?
3) Any hard constraint on data residency other than US?

Next steps: 
- I'll loop in our security/compliance lead (Neha) and solutions lead (Aditya) to confirm the artifacts and timelines.
- I'll send the SOC2 redacted PDF, BAA template, network diagram, and a short comparison doc by EOD tomorrow (18/Jun).
- Recommend a 30-minute follow-up with your security team on Wed or Thu to walk through the evidence.

If Wednesday works, propose 10:00am PT / 1:00pm ET on 20 Jun.

Thanks — Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf (will attach), Redwood_BAA_template_v3.docx (will attach), redwood-network-diagram.png (will attach)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: FW: Follow-up from today's call — deployment constraints and evidence asks

Neha — forwarding Cara's note and my reply. Short ask below: can you confirm which artifacts we can deliver immediately, plus any gaps that require a longer run (e.g., custom attestations, audit extracts)? Also advise on whether Dedicated + BAA typically satisfies customers like MedAxis, or whether Private VPC/on-prem is the safer route given PHI.

Quick context: steady ~200 QPS, peak ~1.2k QPS. They prefer Private but want cost/timeline delta.

Specific requests if you can: 
- Confirm availability of a redacted SOC2 Type II PDF and a SOC2 evidence extract (controls/attachments list) we can share.
- Confirm BAA template version & whether we can pre-sign a draft for procurement.
- Provide a short note on network controls for Dedicated vs Private (VPC peering, IP allowlists, private control plane).
- Estimate provisioning timelines: Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs Private VPC vs on-prem (assuming standard onboarding).

If helpful I can set a 20-min sync with Cara + Rajiv tomorrow at 10am PT; they asked for a walkthrough.

Cheers,
Lukas

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: Follow-up from today's call — deployment constraints and evidence asks

Lukas / Aditya — quick answers below; happy to jump on the Wed 20 Jun 10:00am PT call.

What we can deliver now (standard package):
- Redacted SOC2 Type II PDF (attestation) — Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf
- SOC2 control mapping (CSV) and short evidence extract for host/network/encryption controls — will provide summary in the drive folder (link to follow).
- Standard BAA template (editable) — Redwood_BAA_template_v3.docx. Legal can pre-populate a few fields but MedAxis legal needs to sign.
- Network diagram and VPC peering config notes — redwood-network-diagram.png + config checklist.
- KMS integration notes (we support customer KMS via IAM roles; HSM/bring-your-own-HSM needs a short implementation cycle and is supported for Private deployments).

Dedicated vs Private (short):
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity): often acceptable if MedAxis signs the BAA and we enable VPC peering + strict network ACLs. Pros: faster provisioning (typically 2–3 weeks), lower operational lift for the customer. Cons: Redwood retains the control plane; some customers view that as a risk for PHI.
- Private VPC: stronger isolation, private control plane, customer-managed networking. Pros: preferred by security teams processing PHI. Cons: longer lead time (4–8 weeks typically) and a higher monthly baseline.
- On-prem: supported via our Private on-prem package but requires hardware validation and on-site network work (8–12 weeks typical).

Evidence gaps / custom asks:
- If MedAxis requires raw audit logs or specific evidence artifacts beyond the SOC2 extract (e.g., specific host-level logs), that may require an evidence request run (2–3 weeks).
- If they need HSM-backed key material on day one, we should plan for a short engineering sprint (1–2 weeks) for key provisioning & testing.

Attachments I'll drop in the drive: SOC2 PDF, BAA template, network diagram, KMS notes.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf, Redwood_BAA_template_v3.docx, redwood-network-diagram.png

Lukas / Cara — thanks for the quick turnaround and for offering the Wed walkthrough. A couple of notes from procurement/security: 

- Procurement timeline: MedAxis procurement can review a draft SOW + BAA in parallel; internal approval target 3 weeks (we need a commercial + security packet).
- For now we prefer Private VPC, but we will review Dedicated if the cost delta is material and the BAA + VPC peering controls are demonstrated.
- Can you provide a rough cost delta (monthly) between Dedicated and Private for the expected profile (200 QPS steady, 1.2k QPS peak)? Also an estimated one-time onboarding fee for Private and for on-prem.

If you can share those numbers prior to Wed it will speed decisioning. We attached our procurement intake form — please confirm any missing fields.

Thanks — Rajiv

Rajiv / Cara — great, thanks. Affirming next steps and what we'll send by EOD Tue: 

1) Evidence pack: redacted SOC2 PDF, SOC2 control mapping summary, BAA template, network diagram, KMS/HSM notes (Drive link will be shared).
2) Cost estimate (ballpark):
   - Dedicated (reserved pool): estimated $28k/month + no onboarding fee; supports your steady/peak profile with autoscaling headroom.
   - Private VPC (private control plane & reserved infra): estimated $45k/month + one-time onboarding $18k (network peering, private control plane setup).
   - On-prem (customer-hosted appliances): one-time onboarding and hardware validation estimate $120k–$150k + variable ops support.
3) Timeline: Dedicated provisioning 2–3 weeks; Private VPC 4–8 weeks; On-prem 8–12 weeks.
4) We'll prepare a short 30-min walkthrough for Wed 20 Jun 10:00am PT / 1:00pm ET to review the evidence and answer technical questions (Neha and Aditya joining).

If those ballparks look reasonable I'll convert them into a formal quote and a draft SOW for your procurement team to review.

Thanks — Lukas
